newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. Chubb sees insurance axis shifting to Asia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Chubb sees insurance axis shifting to Asia.

text.p: U.S. insurance group Chubb Corp plans to establish strong bases in India, Indonesia and China, which it sees emerging as the focus of Asia's insurance industry, a top company official said on Tuesday.
"The 21st century will be the Asian century. ...India, China and Indonesia will be very exciting," Percy Chubb III, vice-chairman of the group, told Reuters in an interview.
Chubb was in India to sign a memorandum of understanding with local firm Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd to set up a joint venture once New Delhi frees the insurance sector from state control.

Few people in India, Indonesia or China have been exposed to modern insurance practices, Chubb said, but all global players will begin to feel the pressure of competition in these countries by the year 2000.
"If we can get into these markets now it will keep us busy for a few years. After that we will have to consolidate ourselves," Chubb said.

India is expected to open up its insurance sector in a year. State-run giants General Insurance Corp of India and the Life Insurance Corp of India currently have a stranglehold on the market, but many analysts say they offer largely outdated products.
Chubb Corp plans to set up a liaison office in India in a few months' time, with senior executive Mark Mileusnic as country manager.
The group estimates the size of the initial Indian market for property and casualty insurance at about $2 billion. Chubb himself sees it growing to around $12.5 billion in a few years time.
"It must be at least five percent of the U.S. market," Chubb said. The U.S. insurance market is estimated at $500 billion, with about half in the non-life segment.
Chubb is also planning to open a representative office in Indonesia and is scouting for a local partner with which to set up a joint venture.
Chubb says he expects most Asian economies to liberalise the industry and invite more expertise from global insurance firms.
"Five years ago we were very small...but the pattern is changing," Chubb said.
He said his group posted a 30 percent growth in Asian business in 1995.
"We expect to end 1996 with a premium business of $87.5 million in Asia," said Gary J. Owcar, Chubb's managing director and senior vice president for the Asia region.
For the time being Chubb sees his group sticking to coverage of electrical and telecommunications, financial instititions and infrastructure.
Chubb has three representative offices in China but is yet to start direct business. Total Chinese insurance premium business is seen at around $30 billion by 2000.
Apart from American interests, Chubb is also expected to scout for local and overseas Chinese customers.
